# Sampling and Reconstruction of Analog Signals
Generation of a high-rate sampled digital signal as analog and sampling operations by re-sampling this signal at a lower rate in MATLAB

![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/Status-Complete-green)
![Language](https://img.shields.io/badge/Language-MATLAB-orange)
![Application](https://img.shields.io/badge/Application-Signal_Processing-blue)
![Field](https://img.shields.io/badge/Field-Electronics-purple)

## ⚙️ Methodology
* **Reference Signal:** Simulation of a continuous signal (`fa = 100 kHz`) generated by summing three sine waves (300 Hz, 500 Hz, and 1000 Hz) with random initial phases.
* **A/D Conversion:** Subsampling the signal using an impulse train (`fs = 5 kHz`), followed by a zero-order hold (ZOH) and uniform quantization with a step size determined by the input range (`ΔX = 12 V`) and bit resolution (`Nbits`).
* **D/A Conversion:** Reconstructing the quantized signal by applying a zero-order hold followed by a 5th-order Butterworth low-pass filter (`fc = 2000 Hz`).
* **Dithering:** Injecting uniform white noise prior to the quantization stage to evaluate its impact on low-resolution conversions[cite: 1, 2, 3, 4].

## 📊 Results
* **Spectrum and Reconstruction:** Sampling generated spectral replicas at multiples of `fs`, which were subsequently isolated and attenuated by the Butterworth filter, successfully recovering the original waveform.
* **Quantization Error:** Experimental values for mean, variance, and error bounds converged with theoretical models as the number of bits (`Nbits`) increased.
* **Dithering Effect:** Adding noise prior to 4-bit quantization linearized the error and smoothed out distortion steps in the reconstructed signal following filtration[cite: 1, 2, 3, 4].
